title: Ursa: Lightweight Resource Management for Cloud-Native Microservices
problem: ML-driven resource management approaches for cloud-native microservices suffer from lengthy data collection processes and limited scalability. Existing systems must choose between the SLA/efficiency benefits of ML-driven approaches and the speed/simplicity of traditional autoscaling.
motivation: Efficient resource allocation is critical for maintaining SLAs while minimizing cloud infrastructure costs in complex microservice deployments with multi-tier dependencies.
method: Ursa breaks down a system's overall performance target (SLA) into separate targets for each microservice tier, then uses mathematical formulas to calculate how much resources each tier needs. For each microservice, it explores different resource allocations and stops immediately if response time exceeds the tier's target, preventing prolonged performance violations. This approach bypasses the costly data collection that machine learning systems require.
key_novelty: Ursa uses mathematical formulas instead of machine learning to instantly convert a system's overall performance promise (SLA) into per-service resource targets, avoiding expensive data collection and model training.
contributions: Analytical model for SLA decomposition and per-service resource allocation mapping
128× speedup in data collection time compared to ML-driven approaches
43× faster control plane performance than ML-driven systems
9.0-49.9% reduction in SLA violation rates with up to 86.2% CPU allocation reduction
